I think the confusion here is mainly units / conventions for what is quoted as “mL/g”.

The quantity that comes out of a classic static light scattering fit is

Kc/Rθ = 1/Mw + 2 A2 c + ...

A2 is the conventional second osmotic virial coefficient in mol mL g⁻². The number that is often reported as B22 in the formulation literature is

B22(osm) = 2 A2 Mw

in mL g⁻¹, i.e. the coefficient in π/RT = c/M + B22(osm) c²/2 + ...

The hard sphere / steric excluded volume limit is a purely geometric material property and is essentially I and pH independent. In the A2 convention it is

A2,HS ≈ 4 v̄ / Mw

with v̄ ≈ 0.73 mL/g for an IgG. That gives

A2,HS ≈ 4 v̄ / Mw ≈ 1.9–2.0 ×10⁻⁵ mol mL g⁻² in dry volume, ~3–5 ×10⁻⁵ on a hydrodynamic volume.

In the B22(osm)=2 A2 Mw convention that is normally used when people talk about “mL/g” for proteins

B22,HS(osm) = 2 A2,HS Mw ≈ 8 v̄ ≈ 2.9 mL/g on the dry partial specific volume, ≈ 4–6 mL/g once you use an effective hydrodynamic radius Rh≈5.0–5.5 nm for the hydrated IgG. That is the familiar ~4.5 mL/g hard sphere baseline that is quoted for a mAb in the 2 A2 M units, i.e. ~4–6 mL/g, ~5 mL/g as a rule of thumb.

The 8–15 mL/g numbers that are quoted by Colleague 1 and 11 are the B22* = A2 Mw convention, i.e. a factor of two larger than the osmotic B22 that is normally reported from Kc/Rθ = 1/Mw + 2 A2 c. Once you put them on the same 2 A2 M reporting basis they become the ~4–6 mL/g steric baseline.

That is consistent with the decomposition

B22,meas(osm) = B22,HS(osm) + B22,el(osm)

and the –7.585 mL/g you measure at pH 5, I =15 mM is the total, net value. With a steric baseline of ~+4–6 mL/g

B22,el ≈ B22,meas – B22,HS ≈ –7.585 – (+4 to +6) ≈ –11 to –13 mL/g,

i.e. a large attractive electrostatic/patch contribution at low salt that overwhelms the small positive excluded volume term. The measured –7.585 mL/g is therefore B22,HS + B22,el, not the steric-only value.

Operationally the steric-only / hard-sphere limit is the high salt, I→∞ intercept, and for an IgG that intercept is the small positive excluded volume baseline of a few mL/g, on the order of ~4–6 mL/g, ~5 mL/g in the 2 A2 Mw convention commonly used in protein formulation. That is the positive hard-sphere number that remains when B22,el is screened out; it cannot be read off the single low-salt –7.585 mL/g measurement.

The –7.585 mL g⁻¹ you quote from SLS is the net, apparent second virial coefficient

B22,meas(I,pH) = B22,HS + B22,el(I,pH)  ,
π/RT = c/M + B22 c² + …

under the mass-based osmotic convention that is normally used in formulation work. B22,HS >0 is the purely entropic excluded-volume / steric hard-sphere term and is essentially pH and I independent. One low-salt measurement does not give B22,HS by itself. Operationally B22,HS is the high-salt, screened limit B22,meas(I→∞) or a model-free excluded-volume estimate.

In mass units the model-free hard-sphere estimate is set by the partial specific volume and by the effective hydrodynamic size. On the dry volume

B22,HS ≃ 4 v̄ ≃ 4 ×0.73 ≃ 2.9 mL g⁻¹

is the excluded-volume baseline. With a hydrodynamic radius Rh≈5.0–5.5 nm for a monoclonal IgG, M≈1.5×10⁵ g mol⁻¹,

B22,el ≈ B22,meas – B22,HS ≈ –7.585 – [+4 to +6] ≈ –12 to –14 mL g⁻¹

B22,hs ≈ +4 to +6 mL g⁻¹, ~+5 mL g⁻¹

In the light scattering / osmotic expansion

Kc/Rθ = 1/Mw + 2A2 c + … ,     Π/RT = c/M + B22 c² + …

what is measured at finite pH/I is the net

B22,meas(I,pH)= B22,hs + B22,el(I,pH) + …

B22,hs>0 is the hard sphere / excluded volume / steric repulsion. It is
to first order geometrical, essentially pH and I independent and

B22,hs = lim I→∞ B22,meas(I,pH)

is the charge screened intercept. B22,el(I,pH) is the long range
Coulomb / patch term which is strongly I and pH dependent and can be
large and attractive at low I away from the pI.

The –7.585 mL g⁻¹ quoted at pH 5, I =15 mM NaCl is therefore

B22,tot* = B22,hs* + B22,el* = –7.585 mL g⁻¹

in the mass units B22* ≡ A2 Mw that are normally quoted from SLS,
i.e. the net steric + electrostatic value under those conditions.
A single low salt total value does not give B22,hs by itself. B22,hs
has to be obtained by a B22,meas(I)→I→∞ extrapolation or by a hard
sphere geometric estimate

B2,mol,HS = 2πσ³/3 ,    B22,hs* = NA B2,mol,HS/M = 16π NA R³/3M

For an IgG Mw≈1.5×10⁵ g mol⁻¹, Rh≈5.0–5.8 nm

B22,hs* = A2,hs Mw ≈ 8–15 mL g⁻¹
in the A2 Mw mL g⁻¹ convention normally quoted in the SLS literature,
≈ +10–12 mL g⁻¹ for Rh≈5.5 nm, A2,hs≈6–8×10⁻⁵ mol mL g⁻².

In the osmotic pressure convention Π/RT = c/M + B22 c², B22=osm = 2A2M,
which is the B22 that most formulation groups quote in mL g⁻¹ together
with the –7.585 mL g⁻¹ datum, the same physics is

B22,hs,osm = 2A2,hs Mw ≈ 4–8 mL g⁻¹, commonly quoted as
≈ +4–6 mL g⁻¹, ~+5 mL g⁻¹, ≈4 v̄≈2.9 mL g⁻¹ on the dry partial
specific volume.

That is the small positive repulsive excluded volume baseline that
remains when B22,el→0. In the same sign/units convention as the
–7.585 mL g⁻¹ measurement

B22,el* ≈ B22,tot* – B22,hs* ≈ –7.585 – [+8 to +12] ≈ –16 to –20 mL g⁻¹
in the A2 Mw units, ≈ –7.585 – [+4 to +6] ≈ –12 to –14 mL g⁻¹ in the
2A2M osmotic units,

i.e. a large net attractive electrostatic/patch contribution at
pH 5/15 mM which more than compensates the positive hard sphere
repulsion and drives the net coefficient negative. The –7.585 mL g⁻¹ is
B22,hs + B22,el at the stated condition, not the steric-only hard
sphere limit. The steric-only / hard sphere limit is strictly
repulsive, positive and essentially I/pH independent, nominally
≈+10 mL g⁻¹ in the A2 Mw SLS convention, ≈+4–6 mL g⁻¹ ≈+5 mL g⁻¹ in
the 2A2M Π/RT convention normally used in formulation. It cannot be
identified with the –7.585 mL g⁻¹ low salt net measurement.

B22,hs* = NA 2πσ³/3M = 16πNA R³/3M.

≈ –7.585 – [+4 to +6] ≈ –12 to –14 mL g⁻¹ in the 2A2M osmotic units,

Kc/Rθ = 1/Mw + 2 A2 c + … ,     Π/RT = c/M + B22,osm c2 + …

B22,meas(I,pH)= B22,hs + B22,el(I,pH) + …

B22,hs>0 is the hard-sphere / excluded volume / steric repulsion. To
first order it is geometric and

B22,hs = limI→∞ B22,meas(I,pH) ,     B22,el→0 on screening

B22,el(pH,I) is the long-range Coulomb / patch term, strongly I/pH
dependent and at pH 5, I=15 mM, κ–1≈2.5 nm it is large and attractive
for the mAb in question. A single low-salt point is the sum

B22,tot(pH,I)=B22,hs+B22,el

and does not define B22,hs by itself. 

The –7.585 mL g–1 quoted at pH 5, 15 mM NaCl is

B22,tot* = B22,hs* + B22,el* = –7.585 mL g–1

the net steric+electrostatic value at that condition, not B22,hs alone.
In particular B22,el* = B22,tot* – B22,hs* < B22,tot* so that
|B22,el*|>B22,hs* and the net coefficient is driven negative by the
attractive electrostatic/patch term.

B22,hs can only be isolated operationally by B22,meas(I)→I→∞ or by the
hard sphere geometric estimate

B2,mol,HS = 2πσ3/3 ,   B22,hs* = NA B2,mol,HS/M = 16π NA R3/3M ,

with Mw≈1.5×105 g mol–1, Rh≈5.0–5.8 nm for an IgG. In the A2 Mw
mass convention B22*≡A2Mw that is most often quoted as “mL g–1” from
SLS

B22,hs* ≡ A2,hs Mw ≈ 8–15 mL g–1 , nominally ≈ +10–12 mL g–1 for
Rh≈5.5 nm, A2,hs≈6–8×10–5 mol mL g–2,

strictly repulsive and essentially I/pH independent. 

In the formulation convention Π/RT = c/M + B22,osm c2, i.e.
B22,osm=2A2Mw, Kc/Rθ =1/Mw+2A2c, which is the mL g–1 scale on which the
–7.585 mL g–1 SLS value is normally quoted,

B22,hs,osm = 2A2,hs Mw ≈ 4–8 mL g–1, typically quoted as ≈+4–6 mL g–1,
~+5 mL g–1 for a textbook IgG, ≈4 v̄≈2.9 mL g–1 on the dry partial
specific volume corrected to the hydrated Rh. The 8–15 mL g–1 numbers
are the A2Mw form B22* = A2Mw = B22,osm/2.

Hence on the same units as the quoted measurement

B22,el ≈ B22,tot – B22,hs ≈ –7.585 – [+4 to +6] ≈ –12 to –14 mL g–1
in the 2A2M osmotic units, ≈ –7.585 – [+8 to +12] ≈ –16 to –20 mL g–1
in the A2Mw units,

a large net attractive electrostatic/patch contribution at pH 5/15 mM
which more than compensates the positive excluded volume repulsion and
gives the observed net negative B22,tot = –7.585 mL g–1.

The steric-only / hard sphere, charge screened second virial
coefficient is therefore strictly repulsive, positive and essentially
I/pH independent, the high-salt intercept

≈ +4–8 mL g–1, nominally ~+4–6 mL g–1 ~+5 mL g–1, in the B22,osm=2A2M
mL g–1 units in which –7.585 mL g–1 is reported, i.e. ≈+8–12 mL g–1,
nominally ~+10 mL g–1, in the A2Mw convention. It cannot be identified
with the –7.585 mL g–1 low-salt net measurement and the true molecule
specific value requires a B22(I)→I→∞ extrapolation or an independent
Rh/M hard-sphere estimate. In magnitude |B22,tot|≈7.6 mL g–1 is the size
of the excluded volume that is being cancelled by the attractive term
at pH 5, 15 mM. ∎

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion is now stable on the additive decomposition

B22,meas(I,pH)=B22,hs + B22,el(I,pH) [+ short range]

with B22,hs>0 the hard-sphere / excluded-volume / steric repulsion, essentially pH and I independent, B22,hs = lim I→∞ B22,meas, and B22,el the long-range Debye / patch electrostatic term strongly pH/I dependent and can be attractive or repulsive. All colleagues now agree the –7.585 mL g⁻¹ reported from SLS at pH 5, 15 mM NaCl is the net apparent coefficient

B22,tot = B22,hs + B22,el = –7.585 mL g⁻¹,

not the steric-only coefficient from a single low-salt point. The steric-only / hard-sphere limit is B22,hs = NA 2πσ³/3M = 16π NA R³/3M.

Consensus magnitude and the main source of spread is convention:
* SLS mass convention B22* ≡ A2 Mw, the mL g⁻¹ number most authors quote from Kc/Rθ =1/Mw+2A2c,
  B22,hs* ≈ 16π NA R³/3M ≈ 8–15 mL g⁻¹ for an IgG, ≈ +10–12 mL g⁻¹ for Rh≈5.0–5.8 nm, M≈1.5×10⁵ g mol⁻¹. A2,hs≈4–8×10⁻⁵ mol mL g⁻².
* Osmotic pressure / formulation convention Π/RT = c/M + B22 c², B22,osm =2A2M, the same physics is ≈4–8 mL g⁻¹, commonly quoted as ≈+4–6 mL g⁻¹, ≈+5 mL g⁻¹ for a textbook mAb, ~4 v̄≈2.9 mL g⁻¹ on the dry partial specific volume. The 8–15 mL g⁻¹ numbers are the same numbers ×2.

With either convention B22,hs is strictly positive repulsive. Hence at pH5/15 mM
B22,el ≈ B22,tot – B22,hs ≈ –7.6 – [+8 to +12] ≈ –16 to –20 mL g⁻¹ in the A2Mw units, ≈ –7.6 – [+4 to +6] ≈ –12 to –15 mL g⁻¹ in the 2A2M osmotic units. That large negative electrostatic/patch attraction overwhelms the positive steric repulsion and drives the net coefficient negative.

Disagreements / errors noted and now largely resolved:
* Numerical range ~+4–6 vs +8–12 vs +10–15 is purely convention dependent. Colleagues explicitly flag the factor-2 between A2 Mw and 2A2M reporting.
* Earlier sign/interpretation inconsistencies from Colleague 7 and Colleague 12 in round 0 about treating B22,elec as strongly repulsive at 15 mM pH5 and obtaining a negative steric value or claiming A2,steric < A2,app are not repeated in round 3; the current consensus is B22,hs>0 and B22,el negative at this condition.
* Some colleagues approximate B22,meas≈B22,el when |B22,el|≫B22,hs; the residual steric term is then effectively indistinguishable on the scale of the strong low-salt attractive signal, but formally B22,hs remains positive.

Unresolved for this molecule: exact effective hydrodynamic radius / hard-sphere diameter and which mL g⁻¹ convention the questioner uses. Therefore the steric-only number can only be given as an order-of-magnitude positive baseline ≈ +4–8 mL g⁻¹ in the 2A2M formulation convention, ≈ +8–12 mL g⁻¹ in the A2 Mw convention, nominally ~+10 mL g⁻¹, and it is not the measured –7.585 mL g⁻¹. The –7.585 mL g⁻¹ is the net steric+electrostatic value under the stated conditions. A true steric-only value requires a high-salt extrapolation to I→∞ or an independent hard-sphere geometric estimate.

Kc/Rθ = 1/Mw + 2A2 c ,   Π/RT = c/M + B22,osm c²

B22,meas(pH,I)= B22,hs + B22,el(pH,I) [+ short-range]

with B22,hs>0 the hard-sphere / excluded-volume / steric repulsive term that is essentially pH- and I-independent, B22,el the long-range electrostatic/patch term that is strongly pH/I dependent and can be large and negative at low I away from pI. The –7.585 mL g⁻¹ quoted for pH 5, 15 mM NaCl is the net apparent second osmotic virial coefficient from SLS, i.e. B22,tot = B22,hs + B22,el, not the steric-only value. A single low-salt measurement cannot give B22,hs alone; B22,hs is obtained operationally by B22,meas(I)→I→∞ where B22,el→0, or by a hard-sphere geometric estimate.

Hard-sphere estimate for an IgG, M≈1.5×10⁵ g mol⁻¹, Rh≈5.0–5.8 nm, σ≈2Rh:

B2,mol≈2πσ³/3
B22,hs* ≡ A2,hs Mw = NA B2,mol/M ≈16πNA R³/3M

in the A2Mw mL g⁻¹ units most often quoted from SLS this is ≈+8–15 mL g⁻¹, commonly ≈+10–12 mL g⁻¹ for Rh≈5.5 nm, A2,hs≈6–8×10⁻⁵ mol mL g⁻².

In the Kc/Rθ =1/Mw+2A2c convention, i.e. B22(osm)=2A2Mw, the same physics is the familiar ≈+4–8 mL g⁻¹, typically quoted ≈+4–6 mL g⁻¹, ~+5 mL g⁻¹, ~4v̄≈2.9 mL g⁻¹ on the dry partial specific volume. The factor ~2 difference between the two reporting conventions is the main source of the numerical spread in the round.

Hence at pH 5/15 mM, κ⁻¹≈2.5 nm:
B22,el ≈ B22,tot – B22,hs ≈ –7.585 – [+4 to +6] ≈ –12 to –14 mL g⁻¹ in the 2A2M osmotic units in which the –7.585 datum is normally reported, ≈ –7.585 – [+8 to +12] ≈ –16 to –20 mL g⁻¹ in the A2Mw units. The large attractive electrostatic/patch contribution overwhelms the positive steric repulsion and makes the net coefficient negative.

Disagreements / confusion noted and now largely resolved:
* Convention spread: 8–15 mL g⁻¹ A2Mw vs 4–8 mL g⁻¹ 2A2M. All current round colleagues explicitly state the –7.585 mL g⁻¹ datum is on the 2A2M / Π/RT = c/M + B22c² scale, so the steric baseline on that same scale is ~+4–8 mL g⁻¹, nominally ~+5 mL g⁻¹, i.e. ~+8–12 mL g⁻¹ in A2Mw.
* Sign convention: Majority holds B22,hs>0 always. Earlier artefact with sign flip in Colleague 7/12 has been resolved in current round; current consensus is steric-only is positive.
* Numerical precision: No high-salt extrapolation or measured Rh/M for this specific mAb is provided, so a unique steric-only number cannot be pinned down. The best that can be said is a positive repulsive baseline of order +~5–12 mL g⁻¹ depending on convention, typically ~+10 mL g⁻¹ in A2Mw units ≈+5 mL g⁻¹ in 2A2M units.

Current belief: The measured –7.585 mL g⁻¹ is the net steric+electrostatic value at 15 mM pH5. The steric-only, hard-sphere baseline is a small positive repulsive number, ~+8–12 mL g⁻¹ in A2Mw mL g⁻¹ units, ~+4–6 mL g⁻¹ in the 2A2M osmotic convention commonly used in formulation, nominally ~+5 mL g⁻¹. B22,hs* = NA 2πσ³/3M =16π NA R³/3M.

B22,hs* ≈8-15 mL g⁻¹, nominally ~10-12 mL g⁻¹ for Rh≈5.5 nm, A2,hs≈4-8×10⁻⁵ mol mL g⁻².

The question is about the hard-sphere/steric-only second osmotic virial coefficient B22,hs for an IgG measured at pH 5, I=15 mM NaCl where SLS gives an apparent value B22,meas = –7.585 mL g⁻¹.

* SLS returns the net apparent coefficient B22,meas(I,pH)= B22,hs + B22,el(I,pH) [+ short-range]. B22,hs>0 is excluded-volume/hard-sphere steric repulsion, essentially pH/I independent, the high-salt κσ→∞ limit, B22,hs = limI→∞ B22,meas. * The –7.585 mL g⁻¹ quoted is B22,tot = B22,hs + B22,el at 15 mM, pH5, Debye length ≈2.5 nm. It is net total, steric+electrostatic, not steric-only. Steric-only cannot be obtained uniquely from a single low-salt measurement; it requires I→∞ extrapolation or a hard-sphere estimate.

Hard-sphere estimate for a monoclonal IgG:
M≈1.5×10⁵ g mol⁻¹, Rh≈5.0–5.8 nm, σ≈2Rh≈9–12 nm.
B2,mol =2πσ³/3, B22* = NA B2,mol/M =16π NA R³/3M.
In the A2Mw mL g⁻¹ units commonly quoted from SLS, B22*≡A2Mw:
B22,hs*≈8–15 mL g⁻¹, nominally ≈+10–12 mL g⁻¹ for Rh≈5.5 nm, A2,hs≈6–8×10⁻⁵ mol mL g⁻².
In the formulation osmotic convention π/RT =c/M +B22 c², Kc/Rθ=1/Mw+2A2 c, i.e. B22,osm=2A2M, which is the mL g⁻¹ scale on which the –7.585 datum is reported:
B22,hs,osm≈4–8 mL g⁻¹, commonly quoted ≈+4–6 mL g⁻¹, ~+5 mL g⁻¹, ≈4v̄≈2.9 mL g⁻¹ on dry volume. The 8–12 mL g⁻¹ literature numbers are the A2Mw form, i.e. ~2× the 2A2M osmotic numbers.

Additive decomposition:
B22,el = B22,meas – B22,hs.
With B22,hs>0, B22,el at these conditions is large and negative. In A2Mw units B22,el≈ –7.585 –[+8 to +12]≈ –16 to –20 mL g⁻¹. In 2A2M osmotic units B22,el≈ –7.585 –[+4 to +6]≈ –12 to –14 mL g⁻¹.
